community-gardens:
Community gardens are public crop and herb beds on a few streets, and anyone can plant, water and pick there.
The Streets with a Community Garden list shows every street with one, by region, such as Community Gardens and Kipacre Greens.
On the three Herb Gardens streets every bed is an herb bed.
Bring seeds. Crop seeds are sold by the Gardening Tools Vendor and the Gardening Goods Vendor. Herb seeds come from shucking herbs, or now and then from a Dust Trap.
Plant in a clean plot. Crop seeds only go in a crop bed, and herb seeds only in an herb bed.
Water it with a Watering Can. Seeds only grow while the plot is wet. One watering lasts 72 minutes, and a dry plot stops growing until you water it again.
Pick the crop when it is ripe. Without Croppery I (or Herbalism I in an herb bed) you get half the crop.
Clear the picked plot with a Hoe, and it is clean for the next seeds.
Everyone shares the same plots in the public gardens, except the tutorial bed on Doonboggle Trail.
When a crop ripens, the player who planted it has 60 seconds to pick it before anyone else can.
find-things:
Search for it by name: the Streets with… list for it comes first, then every street whose page names it.
Type its name in the Encyclopedia search, for example salmon or metal rock. Plurals work, and one typo is fine.
Open its Streets with… list, such as the salmon list or the Metal Rock list: every street that has it, by region, with how many when a street has more than one.
Pick a street near you. Each street page shows what lives and grows there, and the other lists it is on.
Browse every Streets with… list: gardens, shrines, vendors, subway stations, rocks, trees, animals and more.
An animal or item page says where to find it and what gives it, such as Salmon and Chunk of Metal Rock.
The subway map shows the street each station comes up on.
get-visitors:
Choose Get visitors at any Visiting Stone, and players who press Visit on a stone can be sent to your home street.
Reach level 4.
Have your home street.
Cultivate 3 items on your home street.
Unbox your Butler. Its Special One-Time Delivery turns up on your home street once you have a home and reach level 3.
Each thing you set down in Cultivate mode on your home street counts as one: a Patch, a rock, a garden, a Dirt Pile, a Firefly Hive and the rest. Things in your back yard do not count.
Open Cultivate mode with the Cultivate button on your home street, or press Shift+C. Each thing costs iMG, and the price grows with each one you add.
Walk up to a Visiting Stone and choose Get visitors. Stop random visitors opts you out again.
Anyone who chooses Visit at a stone goes to the home street of a random player who opted in.
Friends can also come any time with Visit Home Street, from your name or their buddy list, and a house key lets them inside.
With no other players, Get visitors needs level 4, a home and your Butler. A neighbour then drops by your home street each new game day and leaves a gift with your Butler.
house-floors:
Set a Door down on the top floor of your house: that starts the Build a New Floor project, and 100 Planks finish it.
Get a Door. No vendor sells one: make it with a Construction Tool from 8 Wood Posts, 16 Boards and 20 Snails. The recipe needs Engineering and Furnituremaking II.
In your house, set the Door down on your top floor. That starts the Build a New Floor project.
Bring 100 Planks to the project.
When it is done, the Door is the way up, and a Door down stands in the same place on the new floor. A house can have up to 3 floors.
Yes, sideways: drag a placed Door left or right along its own floor, in Decoration Mode or by dragging it in your house. It stays inside the walls and never goes up, down or to another floor.
Each Door of a pair keeps its own spot, and going through one lands you at the other, wherever it stands.
You can only pick a Door back up before its project starts. After that, and on every finished floor, it slides but never comes up.
Expanding works on every floor at once, so each new wall segment takes one Wall Segment per floor. On two floors it also takes an Urth Block; on three floors, 3 of them. Every fourth segment on more than one floor also takes Girders.
learning-time:
Once you know more skills than your brain capacity, which starts at 20, each skill past it makes the next one take 5% longer, and that adds up.
Your very first skill takes only 15% of its usual time.
Skills you know and the one you are learning count against your brain capacity of 20.
Past it, the time grows by 5% for each skill over, on top of the last: 10 over is about 63% longer.
Raise your capacity with Brain Capacity cards: each adds 1, 3 or 5, up to 60. They join your Imagination hand after the First Eleven achievement.
Learn Better Learning I to Better Learning V: the ranks take 2%, 5%, 8%, 12% and then 20% off every skill you learn after them.
Learning Speed cards take time off every skill of one kind.
Spend favor at a Giant's shrine while you learn: each point takes 10 seconds off with the skill's main Giant, 7 with its second Giant and 5 with any other. One spend cuts at most half the time left. An emblem spends as 1,000 favor.
wine-of-the-dead:
Hell's Bartender in the Hell Bar swaps one Diabolical Drink Ticket for one Wine of the Dead, and you get a ticket when someone mourns or celebrates your grave while you are dead.
Croak. When your energy runs out you die, leave a Graveside Marker where you fell, and wake in Hell One in Naraka.
Wait to be recognised. While you are still dead, a companion may walk past your grave and Mourn or Celebrate it, 20 to 50 seconds after you croak. Until you finish Beelzebooze this happens every time you croak; after that, one croak in 3. Online, another player who finds your grave can do it too.
Get a ticket. The first time, you are offered It's Better in a Hell Hole: jump down the Hell Hole. Finishing it offers Beelzebooze, which gives you your first Diabolical Drink Ticket. After that, each recognition gives you a ticket.
Trade it. Go to Panka Surazu at the far end of Naraka, step into the Hell Bar, and choose Buy wine at Hell's Bartender. One ticket buys one bottle.
In Naraka, drinking it takes away Pooped.
Drinking it among the living kills you.
It does not bring you back to life: squish 11 bunches of Hellish Grapes for that.
Beelzebooze ends when you drink your first bottle, for 250 iMG and 150 currants.
On your home street, pouring it on something you cultivated wears it out.
